comparison: Both evaluate claims C1-C4, C12 (OpenEval) and C1-C18 (peer) about Tll/Bsh expression patterns and HDTF temporal expression. OpenEval focuses on immunostaining validation of LPC markers, while peer review encompasses broader temporal expression data (C5-C18). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes work is 'very strong and interesting' with 'convincing series of experiments.'

OpenEval R2 addresses C5-C18 on temporal HDTF expression and classification of primary vs. secondary HDTFs. Peer R1 also covers C5-C18 as part of broader evaluation (C1-C18). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review states authors 'convincingly describe the sequential expression and activity of Bsh...and of Ap' and that 'hierarchical interactions...are well established experimentally.'

Perfect overlap on C19-C21 regarding temporal control experiments with Gal80ts and R27G05-Gal4 driver validation. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes technical validation of LPC driver specificity. Peer review accepts findings but notes concern about figure presentation clarity and requests genetic drivers be adequately noted in panels.

High overlap on C22-C28 regarding Bsh loss-of-function eliminating Ap/Pdm3 while maintaining neuron number. OpenEval covers C22-C28, peer covers C22-C23, C24-C25, C27-C28 (missing C26). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes 'somatic CRISPR knockout of Bsh seems to have a weaker phenotype than the knockdown using RNAi' and requests explanation.

Perfect overlap on C29 regarding Bsh knockout in L4 neurons maintaining Ap expression. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with caveat that autoregulation inference is reasonable but not directly proven. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 raising significant concern about reconciling continuous Bsh expression/binding with lack of requirement for fate maintenance, finding the experiment 'a little unsatisfying.'

Perfect overlap on C30-C38 regarding fate transformation in Bsh-KD showing ectopic L1/L3 markers and morphology. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes mutually exclusive marker expression excluding hybrid fates. Peer review states findings are 'striking' but notes concern about whether 'Tll+/Bsh+ LPCs are the precursors of L4/L5' based on morphological positioning.

Perfect overlap on C39-C41 comparing Bsh-KD and Ap-KD phenotypes to demonstrate fate repression is Bsh-specific. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes that Ap-KD does not cause ectopic L1/L3 markers. Peer review accepts this as part of the hierarchical model showing differential roles of Bsh and Ap.

OpenEval R8 covers C42-C46 on Zfh1 requirement for L1/L3 fate. Peer R7 covers C42-C49, including both Zfh1 requirement and mutual repression with Bsh. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes speculation about additional neurogenesis role. Peer review accepts cross-repression model between primary HDTFs as part of overall mechanism.

OpenEval R9 addresses C47-C49 on ectopic Zfh1 in Bsh-KD and mutual repression model. Peer R7 covers C42-C49 including these claims. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes mutual repression between primary HDTFs explains fate transformations. Peer review states paper 'demonstrates that Bsh in L4/L5 represses Zfh1, which in turn acts as the primary selector for L1/L3 fates.'

OpenEval R10 covers C50-C51, C53-C58 on Bsh:Dam TaDa data and DIP-β binding. Peer R8 covers C50-C51, C55, C58-C61, focusing on DamID profiling approach. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes speculation about Bsh/EcR cooperation lacks direct evidence. Peer review accepts DamID approach but notes 'it is not clear how L4-specific Differentially Expressed Genes were found' and requests clarification.

OpenEval R10 includes C53-C54, C56-C57 on integration of binding data with previous findings. Peer R9 covers same claims. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comparison to C. elegans terminal selectors. Peer review notes 'interestingly, one of these upregulated genes with a Bsh peak is Dip-β' connecting to previous work on L4 connectivity.

OpenEval R11 addresses C59-C61 on chromatin accessibility inference from Dam control. Peer R8 includes C59-C61 as part of broader DamID evaluation. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes speculation about Bsh maintaining Ap through synapse formation is not directly tested. Peer review accepts DamID findings but requests methodological clarification.

Perfect overlap on C62-C66 regarding Bsh regulation of L4 morphology and connectivity. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes inference about additional Bsh targets beyond DIP-β is reasonable but targets not identified. Peer review states work 'proves that Bsh and Ap work in a feed-forward loop to regulate Dip-β expression' but questions why CRISPR-KO was used when RNAi shows stronger phenotype.

Perfect overlap on C67-C69 regarding Ap acting mainly through DIP-β based on phenotype similarity. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges 'mainly' indicates possible additional targets. Peer review accepts feed-forward loop model but notes Figure 6N-R uses LPC-Gal4 instead of L4-Split-Gal4, requesting explanation or repetition with L4-specific driver for accurate comparison.

Perfect overlap on C70-C73, C75 regarding coherent feed-forward loop where Bsh activates Ap and both independently regulate DIP-β. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this constitutes canonical feed-forward loop per cited literature. Peer review strongly supports this, with Reviewer 2 calling it 'a beautiful practical example of the framework of terminal selectors.'

High overlap on C76-C77, C79-C83 regarding behavioral deficits in Bsh-KD consistent with L4/L5 loss. OpenEval covers C76-C83, peer covers C76-C77, C79-C83 (missing C78). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes interpretation about L4/L5 acting together is somewhat speculative. Peer review accepts findings but notes 'it is also possible that L4 activity is dispensable for motion detection and only L5 is required.'

OpenEval R16 covers C84, C86, C88 on main conclusions about hierarchical HDTF function. Peer R14 covers C84, C86, C88, C106, including evolutionary conservation. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes hierarchical function well-supported and conservation speculation reasonable. Peer review strongly supports conceptual framework but notes 'it is necessary to de-emphasize the relevance of HDTFs, or at least acknowledge that other, non-homeodomain TFs, can act as selector genes.'

OpenEval R18 addresses C104-C106 on C. elegans published work and evolutionary comparison. Peer R14 includes C106 as part of broader evolutionary framework evaluation. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes citations are accurate and comparison appropriate. Peer review accepts evolutionary implications as providing 'fundamental insights into the conservation of neuronal diversification programs.'

Perfect overlap on C110-C113 regarding evolutionary model that Bsh expanded lamina diversity from 3 to 5 cell types. OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN, noting model is plausible but lacks direct evidence from comparative phylogenetic analysis. Peer review marks SUPPORTED, calling it 'an intriguing and novel hypothesis that should be tested from an evo-devo standpoint,' accepting it as valuable speculation.

OpenEval R17 evaluates C89-C103 as established background knowledge from cited literature, finding claims SUPPORTED as accurate representations of prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not separately evaluate background literature claims.

OpenEval R19 evaluates C107-C109 on Zfh1-KD reducing non-HDTF targets (Svp, Erm), demonstrating HDTF hierarchy can include non-HDTF downstream targets. Finding is SUPPORTED. No corresponding separate peer review evaluation found, though this concept is implicitly accepted in peer R14's note about acknowledging non-homeodomain TFs as selector genes.
